sections.html:
Selling quickly in Elgin generally means either a cash buyer or a listing that is ready on day one, and condition plus your calendar usually decide between them. With 115,476 residents, buyers and investors are active, but permits, rental licensing and Kane County or Cook County paperwork still decide how smoothly a closing runs.

Elgin straddles two counties, Kane and Cook, so recording and tax bills depend on which county holds your parcel. Check the county named on your tax bill before you contact a recorder.

  • Confirm the parcel number, the county and the township that assesses your home.
  • Request a mortgage payoff figure and look for liens or judgments.
  • Pull permit records for roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces.
  • If the house is rented, learn how the city's rental license treats a sale.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and the lender's review, so the schedule depends on title, payoffs and county paperwork. Ask each buyer for a written offer with a closing date, and compare it with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs.

Older housing is part of Elgin's character. The city has Queen Anne homes built for watch company executives, Sears catalog kit homes from 1908 to 1940, and early cobblestone houses, with two districts listed in the federal register of historic places. Newer housing sits on the west and southwest sides. Downtown has gained townhouses, lofts and condo towers in recent years.

The Fox River Trail, Lords Park (112 acres) and Wing Park (121 acres) give the city parkland that appears in many listings. If your house is in a historic district, say so, since buyers either prize that or worry about exterior rules.

Elgin has 39,317 households with 2.88 people each, and 71.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Owner-occupied homes have a middle value of $273,000, and rent at the midpoint is $1,361 per month.

Treat these as citywide midpoints. Prices near the downtown historic districts differ from prices in newer subdivisions on the far west side.

Five public school districts serve Elgin. Elgin Area School District U-46 covers most of the city, with Elgin High School and Larkin High School in town. Community Unit School Districts 301, 300 and 303 serve western and northwestern pockets.

Commute access is a selling point. Interstate 90 and U.S. 20 cross the city, along with Illinois Routes 19, 25, 31, 47, 58, 59 and 72 and Randall Road. Metra's Milwaukee District West Line has three Elgin stations, National Street, Elgin and Big Timber Road, with service to Chicago Union Station. The Pace bus system meets at the Elgin Transportation Center at 102 West Chicago Street.

Describe the district and nearest station in a listing, since buyers filter on both. A house in a western pocket may report a different district than one near downtown.

Elgin's Community Development Department, at 150 Dexter Court, issues building permits. Review takes about 3 to 5 business days for quick permits such as roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces, 7 to 10 business days for projects needing planner review such as sheds, fences, patios and driveways, and 10 to 15 business days for plans examiner review such as basement remodels, in-ground pools and decks larger than 100 square feet. Applications go to permits@ElginIL.gov.

Work started without a permit can draw a stop-work order and fines, and unpermitted work may have to be removed if it does not meet requirements. If the property is a designated landmark or lies in a historic district, exterior changes require a Certificate of Appropriateness. Elgin keeps an interactive historic property map so you can check an address.

Fixing permit gaps before you list helps, and for houses with several unpermitted changes, a buyer who purchases as-is can take them on directly. Call 311, or 847-931-6001 from outside the city, to find out whether a past project needs a permit record.

sections.h2: Elgin rental license and a sale
sections.html:
Elgin requires a rental license for any residential property occupied by someone who is not a blood relative. Licenses are not transferable and are voided automatically when the property sells, and the new owner has 30 days from closing to apply. Operating without one can bring a $500 citation from Code Enforcement.

Fees depend on unit count. The schedule is $149.00 for one to five units, with one unit inspected. A license lasts one year, and a property that passes its initial inspection with landlord training completed receives a two year extension. For single-family rentals, inspectors review the entire interior and exterior, and any code violation found must be corrected within 30 days or the license can be suspended or revoked.

  • Sellers of occupied rentals should tell the buyer about the 30 day licensing window.
  • Unpermitted changes found in an inspection are subject to enforcement no matter who made them, which concerns buyers.
  • Short-term rentals through Airbnb or VRBO also need the license.

sections.h2: Recording, taxes and utilities at closing
sections.html:
On the Cook side, the state charge is .50 per $500 and the county charge is .25 per $500, and the seller is the liable party. A deed recorded there costs $107. For parcels in Kane County, ask the Kane County Clerk's office for the current transfer declaration and recording fee instructions. Your title company normally manages submissions in both counties.

In Kane County a tax bill follows the property regardless of who owned it during the billing year, so check your closing statement to see whether the seller credits the buyer. A Kane County assessment complaint has to reach the Board of Review within 30 days of the township's published assessment notice. Elgin Township has its own assessor.

For a final meter reading, call Elgin's 311 line, where a Citizen Advocate schedules it for the owner's account. Ask the city at the same time whether any balance must be settled before closing.

Bring the parcel number, the payoff letter and a copy of your latest tax bill to the closing. If the house has a rental license, hand the buyer a copy of the license and any inspection notes so they know what the city will expect during the 30 day window.

faqs.q: Does Elgin charge a transfer tax on home sales?
faqs.a: For parcels on the Cook side the state charge is .50 per $500 and the county charge is .25 per $500. Ask Elgin's Finance Department whether any city-level stamp applies, and have your title company confirm the full charges before you close.

faqs.q: Is my Elgin rental license transferable to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. Licenses cannot be transferred and are voided automatically when the property is sold. The buyer has 30 days from closing to apply for a new license, and the first license year carries an inspection.

faqs.q: How long do Elgin permit reviews take?
faqs.a: Quick permits such as roofs, windows, water heaters and furnaces take about 3 to 5 business days. Planner-review projects take 7 to 10 business days, and plans examiner reviews take 10 to 15. Contact permits@ElginIL.gov for the status of a specific application.

faqs.q: Which county records an Elgin deed?
faqs.a: It depends on where the parcel sits, because Elgin lies in both Kane and Cook counties. The tax bill names the county, and the title company files with that county's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Elgin house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but disclose it and expect questions. Unpermitted work can be ordered removed if it fails requirements. Many sellers close permit gaps first, while an as-is buyer may take on the work and the risk for you.
